title: SSi split-outcome codex, Spanish target side: which side of each structural split a Spanish phrase uses
purpose: The definitions a model (Haiku family) uses to say which OUTCOMES of the pair's structural splits a Spanish TARGET text carries. Tom 2026-10-07 (r-2026-10-07-never-use-regex-to-classify-language): these were target_re regexes in split-matchers.cjs; they are now defined here and classified by a model. One codex per target language because the outcomes are facts about that language's grammar; the id carries the language (S-spa) so a French or Welsh split codex can sit beside it without sharing a cache. Outcome ids (S1A, S1B, ...) are pinned to tools/frame-layer/split-matchers.cjs.
task: You read Spanish phrases from a language course and say which grammatical outcomes they use
request: For EACH numbered Spanish phrase, give the outcome ids it uses, per the codex. Never output O: this codex has no openers.
example: Example: 6: quiero que + subjuntivo 'vengas'; sé (saber) => S1B S9A
general_rules: An outcome is a GRAMMATICAL CHOICE the phrase actually makes: a verb, mood or construction that is present in the Spanish text. Judge the grammar, never a string: 'pide' is pedir, 'piensa' is pensar, 'espero' can be esperar = hope or wait.

Phrases are often fragments (LEGOs and building blocks): 'habría', 'quiero que', 'antes de salir'. Tag the construction the fragment shows. A bare 'quiero que' already shows querer que (S1B) even with no verb after it.
Check EVERY phrase against EVERY outcome; a phrase can carry several outcomes, of the same split or of different splits ('no creo que sepa' fires S4B and S9A). Many phrases carry none.
Accents may be missing in course text ('podria', 'esta'); read the intended word.
When unsure, follow the outcome's boundary rules; if they do not settle it, do not fire.
output: One line per phrase: '<number>: <tokens>' where tokens are outcome ids, or '-' when there is nothing. Example: '12: S1B S9A'.

frames.name: S1 want: querer + INFINITIVE
frames.definition: A form of querer (want) followed directly by an INFINITIVE: the wanter does the action. Includes clitics on the infinitive and negation.
boundary: An infinitive must follow querer (clitics allowed). A bare form of querer with no complement ('quiero', 'quieres') does NOT fire.
'querer decir' (to mean) fires S1A.

frames.name: S1 want: querer que + SUBJUNCTIVE
frames.definition: A form of querer followed by 'que' (and normally a present or past subjunctive): wanting SOMEONE ELSE to do something.

near_misses.why: 'lo que' relative before querer, no 'querer que'

boundary: 'que' must follow querer as its complementiser.

frames.name: S2 hope: esperar + INFINITIVE
frames.definition: esperar meaning HOPE followed directly by an INFINITIVE: the hoper does the action.
positives: esperamos volver el año que viene
boundary: esperar = wait + a + infinitive ('espera a ver') does not fire.

frames.name: S2 hope: esperar que + SUBJUNCTIVE
frames.definition: esperar (hope) followed by 'que' and a subjunctive: hoping SOMEONE ELSE does something or something happens.
positives: espero que tengas un buen día

near_misses.why: esperar a que = wait until, not hope

boundary: Only esperar = hope; 'esperar a que' (wait until) does not fire.

frames.name: S3 before/after: antes de / después de + INFINITIVE
frames.definition: antes de or después de followed directly by an INFINITIVE (same subject).
positives: lávate las manos antes de cenar
boundary: The word after 'de' must be an infinitive (or haber + participle).

frames.name: S3 before/after: antes de que / después de que + SUBJUNCTIVE
frames.definition: antes de que or después de que introducing a clause with its own subject (subjunctive after antes de que; subjunctive or indicative after después de que).
positives: antes de que llegue tu madre

near_misses.why: fixed phrase 'antes que nada', no 'de que'

boundary: Requires 'de que' after antes/después.

frames.name: S4 think that: pensar/creer que + INDICATIVE (affirmative)
frames.definition: An AFFIRMATIVE (not negated) form of pensar or creer followed by 'que' (opinion: I think that...), normally with an indicative verb.

near_misses.why: pensar en = think about, no que

boundary: A question 'crees que...?' is affirmative and fires S4A.
Negated matrix ('no creo que') is S4B, never S4A.

frames.name: S4 think that: no pensar/creer que + SUBJUNCTIVE (negated)
frames.definition: A NEGATED form of pensar or creer followed by 'que' (I don't think that...), normally with a subjunctive verb.
positives: nunca pensé que fuera tan difícil

near_misses.why: matrix affirmative, negation inside the clause (S4A)

boundary: The negation (no, nunca) must govern pensar/creer itself.

frames.name: S5 relative clause: que + INDICATIVE (specific referent)
frames.definition: A RELATIVE CLAUSE introduced by que (or quien, donde, el que) whose verb is INDICATIVE, describing a specific, known referent: 'el libro que compré', 'la mujer que vive aquí'.
positives: el chico que conocí en Madrid

near_misses.text: busco a alguien que hable inglés

near_misses.why: 'que' as a complementiser, not a relative

boundary: Only relative clauses count; complement clauses after verbs (decir que, creer que) do not.

frames.name: S5 relative clause: que + SUBJUNCTIVE (non-specific)
frames.definition: A RELATIVE CLAUSE whose verb is SUBJUNCTIVE because the referent is non-specific, hypothetical or non-existent: 'busco a alguien que hable inglés', 'no hay nada que pueda hacer', 'lo que quieras'.
positives: busco a alguien que hable inglés
no hay nada que pueda hacer
necesito un piso que tenga balcón

near_misses.text: conozco a alguien que habla inglés

boundary: Only relative clauses; subjunctive after a complementiser 'que' does not fire.

frames.name: S6 could: podría (conditional)
frames.definition: A CONDITIONAL form of poder: podría, podrías, podríamos, podrían (could = would be able / polite request / possibility).

frames.name: S6 could: podía (imperfect)
frames.definition: An IMPERFECT form of poder: podía, podías, podíamos, podían (could = was able, ongoing or habitual past ability).

frames.name: S6 could: pudo/pude (preterite)
frames.definition: A PRETERITE form of poder: pude, pudiste, pudo, pudimos, pudisteis, pudieron (could = managed to, on one occasion).

frames.name: S6 could: pueda (present subjunctive)
frames.definition: A PRESENT SUBJUNCTIVE form of poder: pueda, puedas, podamos, podáis, puedan.
boundary: 'podamos' and 'podáis' are subjunctive only when the context requires it; 'podemos' is indicative.

frames.name: S7 double-'d: habría + PARTICIPLE (main clause)
frames.definition: A CONDITIONAL form of haber (habría, habrías, habríamos, habrían), the conditional perfect 'would have'. A bare 'habría' counts.

frames.name: S7 double-'d: hubiera(s) + PARTICIPLE (if-clause)
frames.definition: A form of the IMPERFECT SUBJUNCTIVE of haber (hubiera, hubieras, hubiéramos, hubieran, or -iese forms), the pluperfect subjunctive 'had (done)' in an if-clause or wish. A bare 'hubieras' counts.

frames.name: S8 like: dative gustar (a X le gusta)
frames.definition: gustar in the dative construction in the PRESENT or PAST indicative (not the conditional): me gusta, te gustan, le gustaba, nos gustó, a mi madre le gusta.
positives: a mi hermano le gustaba leer
boundary: Subjunctive 'que te guste' also fires S8A (it is not the conditional).

frames.name: S8 like: me gustaría + INFINITIVE
frames.definition: The CONDITIONAL of gustar (gustaría, gustarían), normally 'me gustaría + infinitive' = I would like to.

frames.name: S9 know: saber (a fact, a skill)
frames.definition: Any form of saber (sé, sabes, sabe, sabemos, saben, sabía, supe, sabré, sepa, saber...): knowing a fact or how to do something.
boundary: Unaccented 'se' is the pronoun unless the text plainly means 'I know'.
'sabe a' (tastes of) does not fire.

frames.name: S9 know: conocer (a person, a place)
frames.definition: Any form of conocer (conozco, conoces, conoce, conocí, conocía, conocer...): knowing or meeting a person, being familiar with a place or thing.
boundary: Adjectival 'conocido' (well-known) does not fire; participle in a perfect ('he conocido') does.

frames.name: S10 ask: preguntar (a question)
frames.definition: Any form of preguntar (to ask a question, ask about): pregunto, preguntó, preguntarle, pregúntale.
boundary: The noun 'pregunta' does not fire; reflexive 'me pregunto' (I wonder) does fire.

frames.name: S10 ask: pedir (for something)
frames.definition: Any form of pedir (to ask for, request, order): pido, pides, pide, pedí, pidió, pidieron, pida, pedir.
boundary: Only pedir itself; despedir, impedir, medir do not fire.

frames.name: S11 personal 'a': a + human direct object
frames.definition: The PERSONAL 'a' marking a human (or personified) DIRECT object of a verb: 'veo a María', 'conozco a tu hermano', 'busco a alguien', 'llama a tu madre'.
positives: busco a alguien que hable inglés

near_misses.text: le di el libro a Juan

boundary: Indirect objects (dar/decir/enviar algo a alguien) do not fire.
'a mi hermano le gusta' (dative experiencer) does not fire.

frames.name: S12 it is: ser
frames.definition: Any form of ser (es, son, era, fue, será, sería, sea, ser, soy, eres, somos): identity, characteristic, time, origin, evaluation.
boundary: 'fue/fueron/fuera' can be ir; fire S12A only when the meaning is 'was/were'.

frames.name: S12 it is: estar
frames.definition: Any form of estar (está, están, estaba, estuvo, estará, esté, estar, estoy, estás): location, state, progressive (estar + gerund).
boundary: Unaccented 'esta' before a noun is the demonstrative and does not fire.
